transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference. Joining me is Devon, our systems engineer.
[00:06] Aria Gomez: Hi, Aria here, CTO at Lyra Systems. Samir and Lena are on as well.
[00:12] Samir Kapoor: Hey.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Hi.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. The goal for today is to understand your networking and security constraints for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. We'll cover VPC peering vs private endpoints, region constraints, and any compliance needs.
[00:30] Devon Patel: Quick intro from me, I focus on infra and will walk through typical topology options and tradeoffs.
[00:36] Aria Gomez: We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary drivers are data residency, no egress of sensitive telemetry, and connectivity to our internal services (feature store, embeddings DB). Also latency is important — sub 50ms for inference ideally for customer-facing features.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Totally. Can you give us your current cloud setup?
[00:56] Samir Kapoor: We're on AWS, multi-account setup. Primary production in us-west-2, secondary in eu-west-1. We use Transit Gateway and have Direct Connect to colo. We prefer private connectivity — VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: Security checklist: SOC 2, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SSO with SAML. Also periodic pen tests.
[01:23] Devon Patel: That's aligned with our Private offering. Typical options: 1) VPC Peering to a Redwood-managed VPC, 2) AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or 3) customer-hosted deployment in your VPC/air-gapped with our private control plane. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:40] Maya Chen: I'll run through the high-level differences. With VPC peering you get low-latency L3 connectivity but we need CIDR non-overlap and routing rules. PrivateLink gives you managed endpoints and tighter cross-account access, works well with Transit Gateway too. Customer-hosted gives you full control but adds ops overhead.
[01:58] Samir Kapoor: Do we need to open any inbound ports to our infra from Redwood?
[02:02] Devon Patel: For PrivateLink it's outbound from your VPC to our service endpoint in the Redwood account, inbound is handled by the ENI created in your subnet; you control the subnets and SGs. For peering you control route tables and security groups; we don't need open internet. Both avoid public internet egress.
[02:21] Aria Gomez: What about region availability? We need the cluster in us-west-2 for primary latency, but want EU for DR. Can Redwood spin up Private deployments in eu-west-1?
[02:33] Maya Chen: Yes, Private can be provisioned in multiple regions. Hosted usually runs in our standard regions, Dedicated reserved pools can be provisioned where we have capacity — we support us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for Private deployments commonly. We'll confirm capacity and SLA in the follow-up.
[02:50] Lena Ortiz: KMS/HSM — can Redwood integrate with our CMKs? We need customer-managed keys.
[02:57] Devon Patel: We support customer KMS via cross-account grants for Private. For on-prem or customer-hosted, we can integrate with your HSM/KMS. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption but customer-managed keys are part of enterprise Private plans.
[03:12] Samir Kapoor: Networking details — we use strict CIDR ranges and have a VPN to colo. If we do peering, are there MTU considerations or performance tuning you recommend?
[03:21] Devon Patel: Good callout. We typically recommend matching MTU and enabling jumbo frames across Direct Connect where possible. For high throughput we can provision dedicated instances and tune batch sizes. We'll share a perf tuning doc.
[03:33] Maya Chen: A common customer pattern is PrivateLink for control-plane connectivity and VPC peering/VPN for data plane, depending on whether you want full private traffic flow.
[03:44] Aria Gomez: What about egress billing or data flow? If we keep all traffic internal, are there AWS cross-account charges?
[03:52] Devon Patel: There can be inter-AZ or inter-region data transfer costs depending on topology. With peering inside same region costs are minimal, with PrivateLink there are interface endpoint charges. We'll include a cost comparison in the pricing follow-up.
[04:06] Samir Kapoor: Can you talk through the authentication flows? We need RBAC and ability to map SAML groups to Redwood roles.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role mapping. For Private deployments we can federate to your IDP or run an enterprise control plane that connects to your SSO.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: Audit logs — we need all request/response metadata logged and forwarded to our SIEM. Are logs stored by Redwood? For compliance we need retention controls.
[04:36] Devon Patel: We persist audit trails and can export logs to your S3 via cross-account delivery, or stream to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch, depending on region. Retention policies are configurable for Private.
[04:48] Aria Gomez: Is there an option to have the model weights behind our VPC, so model artifacts aren't in Redwood's managed storage?
[04:56] Devon Patel: For customer-hosted deployments yes; you can host model assets in your bucket or a mounted volume. For Redwood-managed Private, weights are stored in our managed object store but can be configured with encryption and access controls; we also offer VPC-restricted object access. We'll cover options in the architecture doc.
[05:12] Maya Chen: Let's cover a sample topology — Devon?
[05:15] Devon Patel: (screen share described) Imagine Redwood control plane endpoints reachable over PrivateLink; inference workers run in our managed VPC but we create a VPC peering connection to your prod VPC for direct traffic, or we place interface endpoints in your account to route to our service. In customer-hosted mode, inference pods run in your VPC and you control EKS/instances.
[05:34] Aria Gomez: Latency — you mentioned sub-50ms target. What SLAs and typical p50/p95 latency do customers see?
[05:41] Devon Patel: For small-request chat workloads p50 can be ~20-40ms in-region with Dedicated pools and optimized batching, p95 depends on sequence length; we'll share benchmark numbers. Private deployments in same region usually match Dedicated performance.
[05:54] Samir Kapoor: We care about KV cache locality — does the runtime keep KV cache in-memory in the same VPC or is it remote?
[06:00] Devon Patel: KV cache is local to the worker. For cross-VPC scenarios we ensure workers are colocated in region and AZs to minimize cross-network hops. If you run customer-hosted, KV remains in your network.
[06:12] Aria Gomez: What about compliance certifications?
[06:15] Maya Chen: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and are pursuing ISO 27001; our security package includes the reports, pen test summaries, and security architecture. We'll send the package.
[06:25] Lena Ortiz: Any third-party subprocessors?
[06:28] Maya Chen: We list subprocessors in the security doc and have data processing addendums as needed.
[06:32] Samir Kapoor: If we need to run in govcloud or special regions, is that supported?
[06:36] Devon Patel: We have partners and options for restricted regions; govcloud is possible via a Private deployment or dedicated partner stack. That usually requires extra lead time and contract terms.
[06:47] Aria Gomez: On the networking ops side, what does the onboarding look like? Who sets up VPC peering?
[06:53] Maya Chen: Typically, customer infra creates the peering or accepts the PrivateLink endpoint creation. We'll provide IaC snippets (Terraform) and a network runbook. Devon will help coordinate.
[07:03] Samir Kapoor: We need to know required security group rules and route table changes before we start.
[07:07] Devon Patel: We'll send a checklist: required subnets, CIDR constraints, SG examples, IAM roles, and cross-account roles for KMS.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Any blockers on compliance or legal?
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: Contractual DPA and data residency clauses — we'll need to review. Also need to confirm deletion policies and data access during audits.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Understood. Those are standard for Private — we can include DPA and data processing terms in the follow-up.
[07:34] Aria Gomez: Cost — what's the difference between Dedicated and Private?
[07:38] Devon Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood-managed infra with predictable throughput; Private runs in isolated VPCs (could be Redwood-managed or customer-hosted) with slightly higher base costs due to isolation and dedicated networking. We'll produce a pricing comparison tailored to your workload.
[07:52] Samir Kapoor: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
[07:55] Devon Patel: Sample prompts, typical sequence lengths, expected concurrency, and any safety/filters. We'll run sample runs on a Dedicated pool and on Private to compare latency and cost.
[08:07] Aria Gomez: Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in Q2; can Redwood support a 4-week POC?
[08:14] Maya Chen: Yes, 4-week POC is common. We'll scope success criteria (latency targets, cost thresholds, integration checklist).
[08:22] Lena Ortiz: About logs forwarded to our SIEM — can logs exclude PII and contain only metadata for compliance?
[08:29] Devon Patel: We can configure log redaction and filtering and control which fields are exported. We'll document options.
[08:36] Aria Gomez: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[08:39] Maya Chen: We'll send security docs, network runbook, Terraform snippets, pricing, and propose dates for the technical deep-dive.
[08:47] Samir Kapoor: We'll share CIDR and AWS account IDs and confirm preferred dates for the deep-dive.
[08:53] Maya Chen: Quick recap and next steps — Maya to send security package and architecture diagram by 3/4, Devon to set benchmark plan and schedule deep-dive for week of 3/9-3/12, Samir to share network details by 3/6. Pricing estimate to follow.
[09:09] Aria Gomez: Sounds good.
[09:11] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[09:13] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with the assets.
[09:17] (00:58:00) — call ends

Notes: Transcript has minor transcription noise (names sometimes garbled). References to PrivateLink, VPC peering, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, KMS/CMEK, SAML/SCIM, SOC2, log forwarding and retention, customer-hosted vs Redwood-managed Private options.

Links shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf (placeholder), https://redwood.ai/terraform/private-vpc-samples (placeholder).

Recap (auto): Pilot in Q2, requirements: us-west-2 primary, EU fallback, CIDR ranges and account IDs from customer, SOC2 and DPA review, bench runs for latency/cost.
